# GoSQLX

> High-performance SQL parsing SDK for Go: zero-copy tokenizer, recursive-descent parser, AST, formatter, linter and security scanner. Multi-dialect and race-free.

GoSQLX is a production-ready SQL parsing library for Go with zero-copy tokenization, recursive-descent parsing and AST generation backed by object pooling. It supports 8 dialects (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite, Snowflake, ClickHouse) and ships a CLI (`gosqlx`) for validation, formatting, linting, transpilation and security analysis. Apache-2.0 licensed. Requires Go 1.26+.

Current stable version: v1.15.0
Website: https://gosqlx.dev
Interactive Playground: https://gosqlx.dev/playground/

## Key facts

- SQL dialects: 8
- Built-in linter rules: 30 (L001-L030)
- MCP server tools: 7
- SQL-99 compliance: ~80–85% (estimated)
- QA corpus (v1.14.0): Snowflake 87/87, ClickHouse 69/83
- Performance: ~318 ns/op (~3.14M ops/sec) for a simple SELECT (parse stage) on Apple M4, Go 1.27. This is the parse stage only (pre-tokenized input), not tokenize or end-to-end. Source: BenchmarkPerformanceBaseline, median of 10 runs, re-measured 2026-10-13.

## Documentation

### Getting Started

- [Getting Started](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/getting-started/): Install GoSQLX, parse your first SQL statement in Go, and walk the AST in minutes, with copy-paste examples for the high-level API and the CLI.
- [Feature Tour](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/feature-tour/): A guided tour of GoSQLX features: parsing, formatting, linting, security scanning, transforms, fingerprinting and transpilation, each with a short example.
- [CLI Guide](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/cli-guide/): Reference for the gosqlx command line tool: validate, format, lint, parse, analyze and lsp commands, flags, output formats and CI usage with examples.

### Core

- [Usage Guide](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/usage-guide/): Practical patterns for GoSQLX in Go: high-level and low-level APIs, object pooling, dialect selection, error handling and concurrent use in services.
- [API Reference](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/api-reference/): Complete API reference for GoSQLX packages: gosqlx, tokenizer, parser, ast, errors and models, with function signatures, types and usage notes.
- [Architecture](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/architecture/): How GoSQLX is built: the zero-copy tokenizer, recursive descent parser, AST and visitor pattern, object pools and package dependencies, explained.
- [Configuration](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/configuration/): Configure GoSQLX with a .gosqlx.yml file: format, validation, output and analyze options, defaults, file locations, precedence and CLI overrides.

### Reference

- [Error Codes](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/error-codes/): Every GoSQLX error code from E1001 to E4002 covering tokenizer, parser, semantic and unsupported-feature failures, with causes and suggested fixes.
- [SQL Compatibility](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/sql-compatibility/): Which SQL syntax GoSQLX supports across PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite, Snowflake and ClickHouse, with a dialect coverage matrix.
- [Linting Rules](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/linting-rules/): All 30 built-in GoSQLX linter rules, L001 to L030, with what each checks, why it matters, example violations, fixes and auto-fix support.

### Advanced

- [LSP Guide](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/lsp-guide/): Set up the GoSQLX Language Server for diagnostics, completion, hover, formatting and symbols in VS Code, Neovim, JetBrains and other LSP editors.
- [MCP Guide](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/mcp-guide/): Expose GoSQLX to AI assistants through the Model Context Protocol: available tools for parsing, validating, formatting and analyzing SQL, plus setup steps.
- [Security](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/security/): Detect SQL injection with the GoSQLX security scanner: finding severities, supported patterns, usage from Go and the CLI, and how to report issues.
- [Production Guide](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/production-guide/): Run GoSQLX in production: sizing object pools, concurrency and race safety, metrics and monitoring, error handling, timeouts and deployment advice.
- [Performance Tuning](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/performance-tuning/): Tune GoSQLX for throughput: reuse pooled tokenizers and ASTs, choose the right API, profile hot paths and read benchmark results for your workload.

### Tutorials

- [SQL Validator CI/CD](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/tutorials/01-sql-validator-cicd/): Tutorial: build a SQL syntax validator with GoSQLX and wire it into a CI/CD pipeline so pull requests with invalid SQL files fail the build.
- [Custom SQL Formatter](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/tutorials/02-custom-sql-formatter/): Tutorial: build a custom SQL formatter with GoSQLX by parsing queries into an AST, walking the nodes and controlling keyword case and indentation.

### Migration

- [From JSQLParser](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/migration/from-jsqlparser/): Migrate from JSqlParser to GoSQLX: how Java parsing concepts map to Go APIs, equivalent AST nodes, visitor usage and a step-by-step porting checklist.
- [From pg_query](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/migration/from-pg-query/): Migrate from pg_query_go to GoSQLX: swap the cgo dependency for a pure Go parser, map AST nodes and functions, and handle multiple SQL dialects.
- [From SQLFluff](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/migration/from-sqlfluff/): Migrate from SQLFluff to GoSQLX: map lint rules and configuration to GoSQLX equivalents, compare speed and dialects, and move CI checks over.

### Editors

- [VS Code](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/editors/vscode/): Install the GoSQLX VS Code extension for SQL diagnostics, formatting, completion and hover, and configure the language server for your project.
- [Neovim](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/editors/neovim/): Configure Neovim to use the GoSQLX language server through nvim-lspconfig for SQL diagnostics, formatting, completion and hover, with a working example.
- [JetBrains](https://gosqlx.dev/docs/editors/jetbrains/): Connect JetBrains IDEs such as GoLand, IntelliJ and DataGrip to the GoSQLX language server for SQL diagnostics, formatting and completion, step by step.
